column3: NASB follows the critical text, without “to me”; “punishment” is rendered “judgment,” and “prostitute” “harlot.”
“Sexual immorality” is rendered “acts of immorality” and “immorality.”
NASB follows the critical text; it moves “in the Spirit” before “into a wilderness.”
NASB follows the critical text (“purple and scarlet,” “the unclean things of her immorality”).
NASB puts the name in capitals; “prostitutes” is rendered “harlots.”
“I marveled with great wonder” is rendered “I wondered greatly.”
NASB follows the critical text (“go,” “will come”).
NASB moves “and they are seven kings” to verse 10.
NASB begins with “and they are seven kings”; it follows the critical text (without “and”).
NASB moves “with the beast” before “for one hour.”
NASB follows the critical text (“their power and authority”); “mind” is rendered “purpose.”
NASB follows the critical text (“and the beast”); “prostitute” is rendered “harlot.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the words of God should be fulfilled”); “to do one purpose” is rendered “by having a common purpose.”
